raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

Multiple API workers inheriting one socket share its accept queue. Give each TCP worker a fresh listener on the same endpoint so SO_REUSEPORT can distribute new connections.

The HTTP launcher adds only 8 lines to supply an optional factory. The process manager uses socket contexts and `nullcontext` to close fresh parent handles after spawn while borrowing the default socket. Production diff: **24 additions / 11 deletions**. No new startup rollback or finalizer reordering; baseline partial-start failure behavior remains. Single-worker, Unix-domain and Rust listener policies are unchanged. Keep-alive requests stay with their accepted connection. Model computation and response formats are unchanged.

Part of #57479; updates the existing PR. Open-PR searches for `57479 in:body` and `reuseport` found no duplicate: #39619 concerns IPv6 utilities, #59521 test flakiness and #52464 DP-engine routing.

## Validation

18 relevant tests pass (one unrelated Rust device-inference test deselected on CPU host), covering real-spawn IPv4/IPv6 listener identity, shared mode and CLI listener policy. Lint and mypy3.10 pass. Fresh synthetic CPU/socket ABBAABBA: eight workers, 2,000 fixed 3,500-token responses per run; all 16,000 payload hashes match. Median render tail **4.776 → 1.587 s**. Maximum requests per worker: A [1147, 1005, 1090, 1017]; B [270, 268, 274, 268]. This A/B was run at `bb44573add`; the final annotation/doc-only trim was not re-benchmarked. Shared-host timings are supplementary; this is not a model/GPU or full HTTP-launch benchmark.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/launchers/api_server/test_api_server_process_manager.py tests/entrypoints/cli/test_serve.py -q -k 'not rust_frontend'
.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files vllm/v1/utils.py vllm/entrypoints/cli/serve.py vllm/entrypoints/launchers/launcher.py tests/entrypoints/cli/test_serve.py tests/entrypoints/launchers/api_server/test_api_server_process_manager.py
.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files vllm/v1/utils.py vllm/entrypoints/cli/serve.py vllm/entrypoints/launchers/launcher.py
```

### Historical GPU/HTTP A/B (before this refactor)

The following results belong to previous PR head **377818881b**. They were not rerun on the ownership/lifecycle refactor and are retained as historical evidence for the independent-listener mechanism.

Single-node GPU/HTTP ABBA: four GB200, HY4-preview reduced to four BF16 layers, DP4/EP4/TP1, four default frontends, 250 requests per replica (1,000 total), non-streaming completions with `logprobs=0`. Abort after the average generated length exceeds 3,500 tokens. The pinned serving image is `0fd2e8d503`; B ports only the exact reviewed listener block onto that image. This is distinct from the PR's main base `94f4170df3`.

| Run | Mean tokens | Requests per frontend (sorted) | Last server serialization | Last client body received | Pause HTTP |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|
| A1 | 3731.648 | 39 / 169 / 289 / 503 | 8.298 s | 9.463 s | 9.857 s |
| B1 | 3633.930 | 240 / 242 / 257 / 261 | 4.551 s | 6.687 s | 5.930 s |
| B2 | 3662.330 | 226 / 252 / 254 / 268 | 4.746 s | 6.693 s | 4.430 s |
| A2 | 3681.236 | 40 / 126 / 327 / 507 | 10.698 s | 11.493 s | 0.823 s |

Server serialization-tail median: **9.498 → 4.649 s (51.1% lower)**. Client last-body-received median: **10.478 → 6.690 s (36.1% lower)**. The median token counts differ by 1.6%; these are raw timings, not equal-token measurements. Two runs per arm, no confidence-interval claim or extrapolation to full-model/DP8 latency. Server serialization excludes ASGI send, network and client parsing. Client last-body-received is timed immediately after reading the final response body, before parsing it. The harness also records time until both `/pause` returns and all responses are parsed; that separate metric is capped by pause return in A1 and is not used as client receive latency. Pause HTTP is a separate, highly variable endpoint; no pause-HTTP speedup claim.

All 4,000 responses returned HTTP 200 with `abort`. Per-run token ranges (A1/B1/B2/A2): 3730–3746 / 3633–3646 / 3662–3674 / 3677–3698. Every run had exactly 1,000 running and zero waiting/finished requests before pause, exceeded the token target, and produced 1,000 conversion/render events. Four greedy rank-pinned smoke responses (token IDs and logprobs) matched across all arms. Identical instrumentation and launch settings; harness hashes unchanged throughout. Both arms used lazy safetensors loading and `NCCL_MNNVL_ENABLE=0` after node preflight failures; failed starts are excluded.


AI assistance: Codex implementation; Claude Opus 5.5 and Kimi K3 adversarial reviews passed. Draft pending human per-line review and personally rerunning relevant tests under AGENTS.md; agent-run tests are not human-run tests.

Final trim: factory returns `Any`, matching the existing `sock: Any` contract, and its documentation is one line. The CLI inode assertion remains after adversarial review; no runtime control-flow change.

2026-10-02: removed the newly introduced Linux-only runtime gate at the user’s request; neighboring socket setup already uses SO_REUSEPORT without an OS allowlist. Independent listeners now apply to multi-worker TCP wherever the existing helper supports binding them. Load-distribution performance is validated only on Linux; no claim for other operating systems.

2026-10-02: at explicit user request, removed added try/except rollback, restored baseline finalizer placement and deleted the seven tests for that removed guarantee. Scoped parent-handle cleanup remains; no immediate cleanup guarantee for partially started worker groups. Historical benchmark data was not rerun after this scope change.

This pull request has merge conflicts that must be resolved before it can be
merged. Please rebase the PR, @aoshen02.

https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/working-with-forks/syncing-a-fork

> Thanks @aoshen02 I only just noticed this... great catch!
> 
> I did a bit more rework/simplification here: [njhill@197ffaa](https://github.com/njhill/vllm/commit/197ffaa9430c1b99c76351e56d425e5737ad9699)
> 
> Please feel free to cherry-pick if it looks good to you.
> 
> Would be good to get this merged asap :)

Agent catch one thing maybe better:
Why this pr is sometimes slower

Think of 8 checkout counters and a crowd of customers.

Today (shared socket): there is one line, and whichever cashier calls "next" first takes the customer. A fast cashier can grab a whole batch at once, so one counter gets crowded while others sit idle. That is the 503 vs 39 requests per server in the PR.
With [vllm-project/vllm#58278](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58278) (SO_REUSEPORT): there is no line. Each customer goes to a counter picked at random by a hash of their connection. Nobody can grab a batch, but random assignment sometimes sends several customers to the same counter by chance.

Which one is worse depends on how many customers each counter gets:

Many per counter (hundreds): random assignment comes out nearly even, about 10% above average at most. Batch-grabbing can put twice the average on one counter. So [vllm-project/vllm#58278](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58278) wins clearly.
Few per counter (one or two): batch-grabbing barely happens; at most 2 per counter in our test. Random assignment can easily put 3 on one counter. So [vllm-project/vllm#58278](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58278) can be a little slower.

Each Python server renders large responses one at a time, so the total time is set by the busiest server. One extra request there costs about 4.6 s. Our n32 test (32 requests on 32 servers) was the "few per counter" case, which is why it came out about 1–2 s slower.

In one line: [vllm-project/vllm#58278](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58278) stops one server from grabbing too much, at the cost of random clumping. It helps under high load and can lose slightly under low load.

Plan

Keep [vllm-project/vllm#58278](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58278). It fixes a real, large problem under high load and is only +24/−11 lines. Add one sentence to the PR description saying when it helps: many connections per server. Also say that with one or two requests per server it can be slightly slower because of random clumping.
Measure it at our real scale (dp-round12, running). DP8 sends 256 requests to 64 servers, about 4 per server. My prediction is that random and shared will be similar here: a busiest server of about 9–10 vs the measured 7–13. The result will replace the old DP4 numbers in the PR.
The simplest real fix is round-robin, not random. Send request 1 to server 1, request 2 to server 2, and so on. Then no server gets more than one request above the others. The easiest way is for the client to rotate across each server's own port, or to put a least-connections load balancer in front. I'll list this as an open question in the RFC rather than build it now.
It doesn't matter for the RL path. With the compact format each request takes about 0.1 s, so one extra request on a server is invisible. The Rust frontend is a single process and is not affected.
Thanks @aoshen02 I guess best would be to benchmark with some realistic high load.
@aoshen02 I guess this can be closed now that https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60723 is merged?

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Thanks @aoshen02 I only just noticed this... great catch!

I did a bit more rework/simplification here: https://github.com/njhill/vllm/commit/197ffaa9430c1b99c76351e56d425e5737ad9699

Please feel free to cherry-pick if it looks good to you.

Would be good to get this merged asap :)

+        create_server_socket(("127.0.0.1", 0), reuse_port=True) as sock,
+        patch("vllm.entrypoints.cli.serve.signal.signal"),
+        patch("vllm.entrypoints.cli.serve.setup_multiprocess_prometheus"),
+        patch("vllm.entrypoints.cli.serve.envs.VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND", False),
+        patch(
+            "vllm.entrypoints.cli.serve.setup_server", return_value=("http://", sock)
+        ),
+        patch(
+            "vllm.entrypoints.cli.serve.vllm.AsyncEngineArgs.from_cli_args"
+        ) as engine,
+        patch("vllm.entrypoints.cli.serve.Executor.get_class"),
+        patch("vllm.v1.engine.utils.get_engine_zmq_addresses", return_value=addresses),
+        patch("vllm.entrypoints.cli.serve.launch_core_engines") as launch,
+        patch("vllm.entrypoints.cli.serve.APIServerProcessManager") as manager,
+        patch("vllm.entrypoints.cli.serve.wait_for_completion_or_failure"),
+    ):
+        engine.return_value.create_engine_config.return_value = config
+        launch.return_value.__enter__.return_value = engine_launch
+        manager.return_value.gather_actual_addresses.return_value = (
+            addresses.inputs,
+            addresses.outputs,
+        )
+        instance = manager.return_value
+
+        def make_manager(**kwargs):
+            factory = kwargs["socket_factory"]

+                    )

+            return instance
+
+        manager.side_effect = make_manager
+        run_multi_api_server(args)
+        instance.shutdown.assert_called_once()

+def test_reuseport_workers_have_independent_accept_queues(
+    host, num_servers, reuse_port
+):
+    """Duplicating one fd must not defeat kernel REUSEPORT load distribution."""
+    from tests.entrypoints.launchers.api_server._api_server_spawn_workers import (

+            ),
+        )
+        try:
+            listeners = []
+            for pipe in manager._address_pipes:
+                assert pipe.poll(30), "Worker did not report its listener"
+                listeners.append(pipe.recv())
+            assert all(bound_address == address for bound_address, _ in listeners)
+            inodes = {inode for _, inode in listeners}
+            if num_servers > 1 and reuse_port:
+                assert len(inodes) == num_servers
+                assert parent_inode not in inodes
+                assert not sock.getsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_ACCEPTCONN)

Nobody can grab a batch, but random assignment sometimes sends several customers to the same counter by chance.

Which one is worse depends on how many customers each counter gets:

Many per counter (hundreds): random assignment comes out nearly even, about 10% above average at most. Batch-grabbing can put twice the average on one counter. So [vllm-project/vllm#58278](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58278) wins clearly.
Few per counter (one or two): batch-grabbing barely happens; at most 2 per counter in our test. Random assignment can easily put 3 on one counter. So [vllm-project/vllm#58278](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58278) can be a little slower.

Each Python server renders large responses one at a time, so the total time is set by the busiest server. One extra request there costs about 4.6 s. Our n32 test (32 requests on 32 servers) was the "few per counter" case, which is why it came out about 1–2 s slower.

In one line: [vllm-project/vllm#58278](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58278) stops one server from grabbing too much, at the cost of random clumping. It helps under high load and can lose slightly under low load.

Plan

Keep [vllm-project/vllm#58278](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58278). It fixes a real, large problem under high load and is only +24/−11 lines. Add one sentence to the PR description saying when it helps: many connections per server. Also say that with one or two requests per server it can be slightly slower because of random clumping.
Measure it at our real scale (dp-round12, running). DP8 sends 256 requests to 64 servers, about 4 per server. My prediction is that random and shared will be similar here: a busiest server of about 9–10 vs the measured 7–13. The result will replace the old DP4 numbers in the PR.
The simplest real fix is round-robin, not random. Send request 1 to server 1, request 2 to server 2, and so on. Then no server gets more than one request above the others. The easiest way is for the client to rotate across each server's own port, or to put a least-connections load balancer in front. I'll list this as an open question in the RFC rather than build it now.
It doesn't matter for the RL path. With the compact format each request takes about 0.1 s, so one extra request on a server is invisible. The Rust frontend is a single process and is not affected.
Thanks @aoshen02 I guess best would be to benchmark with some realistic high load.
@aoshen02 I guess this can be closed now that https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60723 is merged?
